stories.headline: Samsung averts 18-day strike with profit-sharing deal, but bonus inequality triggers internal fractures
stories.summary: Samsung Electronics reached a government-mediated provisional wage agreement with its largest union on May 21, averting a planned 18-day strike by roughly 48,000 workers. The deal grants semiconductor division employees bonuses equivalent to 10.5% of the division's operating profit — potentially up to 600 million won per worker — while workers in other divisions received far smaller payouts, triggering internal resentment and work slowdowns in foundry and packaging units as union members voted on the agreement through May 24. Bank of Korea had previously warned the planned strike could cut 0.5 percentage points from 2026 growth. President Lee Jae-myung publicly rebuked the union during a cabinet meeting for demanding pre-tax profit sharing, signaling government could invoke emergency arbitration if needed.

stories.headline: Starbucks 'Tank Day' campaign triggers national political clash over May 18 commemoration
stories.summary: A Starbucks Korea promotional event called 'Tank Day,' held on the anniversary of the May 18 Gwangju Democratization Movement, sparked a week-long political and public controversy. President Lee Jae-myung condemned the campaign at a cabinet meeting on May 20, calling for 'moral, administrative, legal and political responsibility,' and later criticized a separate 'Siren Event' tied to the April 16 Sewol disaster. Shinsegae Group chair Chung Yong-jin issued a formal apology, and Starbucks Korea's head was sacked. The ruling DPK backed Lee's stance and launched internal campaign boycotts, while the opposition PPP accused the president of overreach and using the issue for electoral advantage ahead of the June 3 elections.

stories.headline: Bank of Korea expected to hold at 2.5% with hawkish signal as won weakness and inflation pressures mount
stories.summary: Ahead of the Bank of Korea's May 28 rate decision — the first under new Governor Hyun Song Shin — analysts widely expected the BOK to hold its benchmark rate at 2.5% for an eighth consecutive meeting while adopting a hawkish tone, with dot-plot projections signaling one to two hikes within six months. The won weakened past 1,510 per dollar on May 22, prompting a joint verbal intervention by the Ministry of Finance and BOK warning of 'excessive' moves. Separately, producer prices reached a 27-year high driven by Middle East war-related oil price surges, Seoul apartment prices accelerated to their fastest weekly gain since January, and household lending growth picked up — all complicating the rate outlook.

stories.headline: Lee attends May 18 Gwangju Uprising 46th anniversary, pledges to enshrine democratic spirit in Constitution
stories.summary: President Lee Jae-myung attended the 46th anniversary ceremony of the May 18 Gwangju Democratization Movement on May 18, pledging to 'definitively' cement the uprising's democratic spirit in the Constitution and secure recognition for overlooked participants. He also visited victims' graves and called for stern punishment of those who glorify state violence or spread disinformation about the uprising — including the 'North Korean involvement theory.' The Democratic Party separately launched legislation to eliminate statutes of limitations for state violence crimes.

stories.headline: Lee and Japanese PM Takaichi hold fourth summit in Andong, agreeing on LNG cooperation and security ties
stories.summary: South Korean President Lee Jae-myung received Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi at a 'state guest-level' welcome in Lee's hometown of Andong on May 19 — their fourth meeting in approximately six months. The leaders agreed to expand cooperation on LNG and crude oil supply, including stockpiling and petroleum product swaps, and held a joint press conference underscoring shared concerns about the security environment amid the Iran war and US-China tensions. The meeting was framed by both sides as a historic marker of rapprochement between the two countries.

stories.headline: Lee calls Israeli interception of Gaza flotilla 'kidnapping,' raises possibility of Netanyahu ICC arrest in South Korea
stories.summary: President Lee Jae-myung condemned Israel at a May 20 cabinet meeting for detaining South Korean nationals aboard a Gaza-bound aid flotilla in international waters, calling the action 'way out of line' and describing it as 'kidnapping.' Lee raised the possibility of Seoul arresting Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu under ICC warrants should he visit South Korea, though framing this as a separate judgment from European countries. South Korea's Blue House confirmed on May 21 that some of the detained nationals had been released. Lee also called Netanyahu a 'war criminal' in related remarks reported by Israeli media.

stories.headline: KOSPI surges 77% year-to-date on AI semiconductor boom; Goldman raises target to 7,000
stories.summary: South Korea's KOSPI benchmark recorded a year-to-date gain of approximately 77% by mid-May 2026, reaching a record high above 8,000 before consolidating near 7,400–7,800. The rally, driven by an AI-led semiconductor boom and shareholder-friendly reforms, prompted a $13.2 billion foreign investor selloff in the week to May 18 and sparked a luxury goods spending surge. Goldman Sachs raised its KOSPI target to 7,000, calling Korea its 'highest-conviction view in Asia.' South Korea announced plans to launch its first single-stock leveraged ETFs on Samsung and SK Hynix.

stories.headline: June 3 local elections campaign officially underway with over 7,800 candidates; DPK and PPP contest key mayoralties
stories.summary: South Korea's June 3 local election campaign officially began on May 21, with over 7,800 candidates registered across the country. The ruling Democratic Party of Korea cast the elections as a mandate for the Lee administration, while internal disputes surfaced — a DPK mayoral candidate in Ulsan suspended his participation in a unified primary over disputed polling. In Daegu, traditionally a conservative stronghold, the DPK candidate's once-favorable position tightened as PPP rallied. Former PPP leader Han Dong-hoon entered the Busan North district by-election as an independent, urging conservatives not to back the PPP candidate. A DPK gubernatorial campaign filed criminal complaints against PPP leader Jang Dong-hyuk.

stories.headline: Lee marks 17th anniversary of Roh Moo-hyun's death, pledging to complete unfinished reform agenda
stories.summary: President Lee Jae-myung attended the 17th anniversary memorial ceremony for former President Roh Moo-hyun on May 23 at Bongha Village in Gimhae, South Gyeongsang Province, alongside Roh's widow, son, and former President Moon Jae-in. Lee pledged to 'resolutely push forward reforms that remove unfair practices and privileges' and to complete Roh's vision of a society founded on fairness and inclusion. The ceremony was covered by multiple Korean and international outlets.

The Diplomat published an analysis of key operational questions for a future OPCON transfer, including ROK Armed Forces command structure reforms. stories.headline: Hanwha unveils KAAV-II amphibious assault vehicle prototype; South Korea targets top-four global defense exporter status
stories.summary: Hanwha Aerospace publicly revealed the prototype of the Korean Amphibious Assault Vehicle II (KAAV-II) on May 18, featuring an unmanned turret with a 40mm CTA autocannon and capability for high-speed water and land transit. Approved development funding stands at approximately $1.78 billion, with initial production planned for 2029 and full fielding by 2036. Coverage linked the reveal to South Korea's broader stated ambition to become a top-four global defense exporter — a goal Lee Jae-myung referenced in his April meeting with Polish PM Tusk — and included a Canadian media tour of multiple Hanwha defense facilities.

stories.headline: North Korea constitutional revisions codify two-state policy; Lee government white paper shifts toward 'peaceful coexistence'
stories.summary: An analysis by 38 North detailed North Korea's latest constitutional revision, which treats South Korea as a separate state across its 'southern border,' removes reunification language, and adds a territorial clause — codifying Kim Jong Un's two-state policy while avoiding explicitly hostile language. Separately, the Lee Jae-myung government published a white paper that reduces references to unification and North Korean human rights and emphasizes dialogue and peaceful coexistence, representing a shift from previous conservative-era posture. Kim Jong Un also convened a military-wide commander meeting, reportedly calling for reinforcement of front-line units along the southern border.

stories.headline: Lee's approval rating holds in the 60s; DPK leads PPP by over 20 points ahead of June 3 elections
stories.summary: Multiple polls released this week showed President Lee Jae-myung's approval rating between 60.5% and 66%, rebounding after a brief dip and attributed partly to positive assessments of economic policy. The ruling DPK maintained approximately 45% party support, while the PPP's rating fell to around 22%. Polls on local election preferences showed DPK candidates favored by 46% versus 33% for opposition candidates, suggesting a favorable environment for the governing party ahead of the June 3 vote.

stories.summary: Hanwha Investment Securities agreed to acquire an additional $433 million stake in Dunamu, operator of South Korea's largest cryptocurrency exchange Upbit, as tokenized securities gained attention. South Korea's Financial Services Commission was reviewing Hana Bank's separate planned $668 million investment in Dunamu under banking-commerce separation rules. iM Bank completed a proof-of-concept for a won stablecoin, and an opinion piece called for progress on a digital asset framework law that has stalled for two years.

Lee announced a government platform for AI-era labor policy, which the ILO chief congratulated and expressed readiness to join. The meeting was covered by both Yonhap and the Korea Times.

stories.headline: Special counsel questions former NIS deputy chief over alleged message justifying martial law to CIA
stories.summary: The special counsel team investigating the December 2024 martial law incident questioned former National Intelligence Service First Deputy Director Hong Jang-won on May 22 over allegations that he delivered a message to the United States conveying justification for the martial law declaration. Hong denied the allegations. The special counsel has booked Hong, former NIS chief Cho Tae-yong, and four other former NIS political appointees on insurrection-related charges, with the investigation expanding following an April raid on NIS headquarters.
